results.correct_value: The P3 slab variation was bolted in 2016 (hazards[0] should say 2016, not 2017). fa and overview left as they are (the credited party's year is sourced 2016 by the ascensionist and 2017 by the route page).
results.evidence: The ascensionist's trip report (climb dated 6/28/2016, posted July 1, 2016) describes installing the belay bolt and the four protection bolts on the slab pitch before the ascent. Independent forum replies from other climbers dated July 2-3, 2016 argue about the newly added bolts, confirming they existed by July 2016. So the bolted slab pitch dates to 2016, not 2017. The route page's 2017 date for the four-person variation FFA is not contradicted by fa's 2016 strongly enough to change fa; only the bolting year in hazards is patched.

results.evidence: Two independent route pages both call for protection to 4 inches: one says pro to 4 inches, the other a rock rack to 4 inches plus early-season axe and crampons. The stored rack and sling_rack already list an optional #4 to cover this, so only gear[0] is out of line.

Sources give different distances: one says downclimb the upper pitch about 20 ft to the first ledge; a trip report says scramble back down about fifty feet to find the slung tree; another route description says downclimb or rappel to about 200 ft below the summit then traverse ~100 ft; others say only 'a short section'. No two agree on a figure. Would settle: two accounts measuring the summit-to-first-anchor downclimb the same way.

results.correct_value: From the top of P5 (Thin Red Line's P7 anchor) rappel this route's own two-bolt anchors with two ropes; on the way, from the top of P3 skip the P2 anchor and go to the P1 anchor, then to the ground.
results.evidence: The first ascensionist's report says that after 5 pitches the line joins Thin Red Line's P7 anchor, and parties can continue or rappel with two ropes from there, skipping the P2 anchor from the top of P3 to reach the P1 anchor; all anchors are two bolts with fixed biners. A separate party (different author) repeating it two weeks later bailed near the top and rappelled the line, having previously rappelled over the upper crack. Nothing supports descending Thin Red Line's M&M Ledge line from this route.
